searchText: I'm interested in getting involed with optimizing the BLS pre compiles You mean writing BLS pre-compile in EVM code? Yep Oh, that's cool notes for last call: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/201 very nice, thank you <@!104006934562107392> Regarding the writing BLS in EVM code, can you self-start on this, or you need some help? I can self start, but certainly some context / links to previous work / pseudocode would be helpful. Have you decided on the language? Heads up that I'm very busy, so this won't be fast it is best to start with Yul, probably it is kind of EVM assembly supported by Solidity compiler Ah, okay. I've heard of it there is definitely no pressure. But it should be understood that if the work goes well, and you are producing good stuff, you should get paid for it so please keep us posted and let us know if you get stuck you can start with Solidity itself, of course, but you will probably find very quickly that you need to drop down to the lower level, which is Yul/assembly I mean you mentioned another language Huff I believe And Solidity isn't very well written for optimization (at least if the assembly output is to be believed) I am not actually familiar with Huff not sure how mature it is I'll look into it but my hunch would be that we maybe should just create a simple language built from assembly for this sole purpose ok Depending how complicated it is, you could just write raw assembly. 😬 (I don't actually encourage this, but it *is* an option) I'm surprised that Yul isn't low level enough. I thought Yul was just about at the metal. Ah, I guess it does try to do some of its own stack management with `let x := ...` raw assembly would work Should I just post here with questions? I don't want to spam the chat yes, why not. If it gets too much, we can create a separate channel, but no need for now as if we have anything else to talk about right now 🙂 I picked a good time, then! Are we sure that the math is optimal? You can find Huff here: https://github.com/AztecProtocol/huff And a good example (for this purpose) written in Huff is weierstrudel: https://github.com/AztecProtocol/weierstrudel which is EC arithmetic for the BN curve Ah, Huff seems ideal It'll have to be patched to include the evm384 opcodes. Also one version of the opcode implementations is here: https://github.com/ethereum/evmone/tree/v0.5.0-evm384-v2 but the interface might change and your feedback could definitely feed into the design
